Internal helper: how the map, label and code parsers name a marker

Source: R/pipeline-internals.R
dot-jst_marker_syntax.Rd

The parse layer's errors about a malformed marker fire before the convention is resolved, and until Session 355 they said "Stata-style missing-value tokens must be '.a' through '.z' (a single lowercase letter after the period)" under every setting – to a user of the sas setting, who types .A, and although a typed marker's case is never refused (the S240 item, finding F1). They are phrased as .jst_phrasing_convention() phrases the refusals that fire before resolution: the per-call convention, else a sas setting, else Stata. "Marker", not "token" (Session 354 retired "token" from the help pages; voice Rule B, S265).

Usage

.jst_marker_syntax(convention = NULL)

Arguments

convention

The caller's per-call convention, raw, or NULL.

Value

A list of strings: rule (the sentence naming the form), one ("a Stata-style missing-value marker (.a through .z)"), some ("Stata-style markers (.a through .z)") and eg ("a Stata-style missing-value marker such as 'else=.a'").
